sections.heading: DirectAdmin limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Panel licence on infrastructure you already run — not Kinsta/WP Engine managed hosting; Does not outrank Plesk (7.4); No published AI story — scored low on purpose because it forces process changes or add-ons around DirectAdmin when infrastructure monitoring is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Personal Plus with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain infrastructure monitoring at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Personal Plus · infrastructure monitoring | Lite | Standard.

Alternative context: unlike Plesk, DirectAdmin is preferable when Admins who want a cheap panel licence on VPS/dedicated they already run because infrastructure monitoring plus infrastructure monitoring match; prefer Plesk when Teams buying managed WordPress hosting (Kinsta / WP Engine) because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for DirectAdmin
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: DirectAdmin is faster for infrastructure monitoring when infrastructure monitoring; log management; hosting control panel; enterprise security and SSO is in-product; skip when Panel licence on infrastructure you already run — not Kinsta/WP Engine managed hosting because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming infrastructure monitoring ownership and WordPress before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Integrations in research: WordPress.

Conclusion: DirectAdmin is worth it if Admins who want a cheap panel licence on VPS/dedicated they already run and infrastructure monitoring are weekly; skip DirectAdmin if Teams buying managed WordPress hosting (Kinsta / WP Engine). That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
